findings.summary: Subjects reference UI promotes hard-coded reference teachers, March 2025 dates, session counts and fallback progress as learner-facing truth when canonical values are missing.
Thesis/Research reference UI seeds a March 2025 reference week, tasks, milestones, chapter percentages, heatmap and 65% KPI and replaces the canonical research renderer.
Existing Subjects and Thesis browser/static tests assert reference sample counts/copy, so regression currently protects mock/stale learner-facing output.
Several Hub projections coerce missing progress to numeric zero rather than an explicit unavailable/stale state.
Presentation code derives research progress from local checklist/UI state; it must remain LOCAL_HUB and must not imply subject mastery or assessment.
Full Hub learner state is stored in localStorage despite the new local canonical storage policy.
Academic diagnostics and scheduler preview/transaction history use direct localStorage and require migration behind one storage facade.
Current backup omits sidecar Hub stores and is not a complete portable recovery bundle.
Standalone credential/current-user compatibility uses localStorage and ordinary backup includes PBKDF2 verifier material.
Schedule/Subjects/Research LOCAL_HUB personal data lives in separate localStorage keys outside the canonical backup path.
Research attachment bodies are embedded as Data URLs in state.researchFiles and require a dedicated binary IndexedDB store plus migration/backup tests.
Global browser keys require scope-aware storage using existing managed/standalone profile authority; no new multi-user/auth feature is authorized.
